summary: Sweat biosensor and team software measuring fluid and electrolyte loss during exercise.
editor_note: Measuring sweat loss is a more useful starting point than prescribing one hydration rule for everyone. The shipping patch links fluid and electrolyte data to individual and team apps, making hardware part of a coaching workflow. Its $10M Series A also funds sensor-free Nix Health. That licensing ambition remains in development and should not be confused with capabilities already delivered by the biosensor.
investors: Shorewind Capital, Great Oaks Venture Capital, Oregon Sports Angels, White Road Investments, Anne Wojcicki, Len Blavatnik

sources.label: Nix Biosensors via Endurance Sportswire funding announcement

product_evidence.claim: The orderable sweat biosensor measures fluid and electrolyte loss and relays hydration data to a phone or compatible watch.
The Nix Pro group app lets team staff monitor multiple athletes, extending individual measurements into a shared coaching workflow.
Sensor-free Nix Health is described as under development for consumer-health platforms, not a shipping replacement for the patch.

market_context.primary_user: Athletes, coaches and performance staff managing individualized hydration.
market_context.differentiation: Measures individual sweat losses and supports team monitoring instead of relying only on population-level intake rules.
market_context.why_now: Financing expands an existing hardware workflow and funds a separate future sensor-free product.

risks.claim: The sensor-free expansion requires validation separate from evidence for the current patch.
risks.basis: The announcement describes Nix Health as in development; shipping hardware does not validate its future algorithm.
